label: definition
statement: On the transient class Z, the chain jumps from i to i+1 and i-1 at rate one each and jumps to a separate absorbing cemetery at rate kappa+v*1_{i=0}, with kappa>0 and v>0. Its transient generator is Delta-kappa I-v|0><0|, where Delta f(i)=f(i+1)+f(i-1)-2f(i).

label: proof
statement: For the two-ended killed walk just defined, lambda=kappa, the class is lambda-transient, and for fixed integers i,j the limit of t^(3/2)*exp(kappa*t)*p_t(i,j) is [max(ij,0)+(|i|+|j|)/v+2/v^2]/(2*sqrt(pi)). This strictly positive kernel has rank two and its {0,1} minor is 1/(4*pi*v^2). It cannot factor as a rank-one product. This rechecks an existing campaign candidate and does not certify novelty.

label: definition
statement: For finite E and orthogonal unit vectors u,v in C^E, the projection law on span(u) chooses singleton {i} with mass |u_i|^2. The law on span(u,v) chooses {i,j}, i<j, with mass |u_i*v_j-u_j*v_i|^2. These are fixed-cardinality determinantal projection laws.

label: proof
statement: For finite E and orthogonal unit vectors u,v in C^E, there is a coupling of singleton projection laws on span(u) and span(v) whose disjoint union has projection law on span(u,v). A capacitated flow splits edge masses q_ij=|u_i*v_j-u_j*v_i|^2 between endpoints with first marginal |u_i|^2. Every required cut holds because its internal mass is U_A*V_A-|c_A|^2<=U_A, where U_A=sum_A|u_i|^2, V_A=sum_A|v_i|^2 and c_A=sum_A u_i*conjugate(v_i).

label: proof
statement: If H=H_1 orthogonal-sum H_2 on a finite ground set and one summand has rank one, the union-marginal coupling exists. Couple the other summand as a subset of a sample from P_H using projection stochastic domination and Strassen. The set difference is a singleton with inclusion masses equal to the rank-one projection diagonal, hence has exactly that summand law. This is a consequence of Lyons (2014), Theorem 2.7.

These examples do not prove the general question.

This refutes this splitting rule, not existence of another coupling.

label: proof
statement: If an automorphism-equivariant factor-of-i.i.d. independent set on the d-regular tree has root density a>0, every b in [0,a] is also attainable by independently retaining its vertices with probability b/a, using an independent label family obtained by splitting the i.i.d. labels. If A is the supremum of attainable densities, the attainable set contains [0,A) and is contained in [0,A]; inclusion of A requires an attainment argument.

label: proof
statement: Suppose for every sufficiently large d the factor-of-i.i.d. density supremum on the d-regular tree is at most (5/4)*log(d)/d, while random d-regular graphs admit asymptotic independent-set density at least (7/4)*log(d)/d. Then the two attainable-density sets differ for those d. The cited Rahman-Virag and Ding-Sly-Sun asymptotics are a local literature lead; their primary statements were not reverified here.

label: proof
statement: The n-vertex lattice trees in Z containing zero are exactly the n intervals [-L,n-1-L], L=0,...,n-1. Uniform L therefore gives exact uniform rooted sampling in expected O(log n) random bits, with a compact endpoint representation of O(log n) bits or O(n) time to list the vertices. Trees modulo translation instead have one class.

label: proof
statement: On Z^d, d>=1, grow a rooted tree from the origin by choosing uniformly from available boundary edges at each step. At three vertices the resulting distribution has total variation exactly 1/6 from the uniform rooted lattice-tree law. With D=2d there are 2D(D-1) equiprobable growth histories, but center-rooted trees have two histories and endpoint-rooted trees have one. This obstruction concerns this uncorrected growth rule.

label: source-limited record or evidence

label: proof
statement: Give each edge of K_n one independent identically distributed continuous weight and retain it if both endpoints rank it among their single lowest incident weights. For n>=2 the graph is a matching, a fixed edge is present with probability 1/(2n-3), and a fixed vertex is isolated with probability (n-2)/(2n-3). The expected number of isolates is n(n-2)/(2n-3); connectivity is impossible for n>2.

label: proof
statement: In the same shared-weight bilateral model with n=6 and k=2, the event that all six edges inside two vertex triples precede all nine cross edges produces two disjoint triangles. It has probability 1/binomial(15,6)=1/5005, yet minimum degree is two. Thus absence of isolates is not a deterministic connectivity criterion. This finite event does not settle the asymptotic fine window.

label: source-limited record or evidence

label: proof
statement: For independent Bernoulli(p) site colours, 0<p<1, boundary incidence patterns [a,b,a,c] and [a,b,c,d] both initially have colour word UUUU but induce different occurrence-colour laws. After exposing occurrence zero as black, occurrence two is black with probability 1 in the first pattern and p in the second. The full-law total variation is 2p(1-p). A colour-word-only state therefore cannot determine label transitions across general nonsimple boundaries; vertex identity or its incidence partition must be retained.

label: proof
statement: Let D=2d. Unoriented simple cycles through a fixed vertex in Z^d have square count 4*binomial(d,2) and six-cycle count 12*binomial(d,2)+96*binomial(d,3). In Q_D the corresponding counts are binomial(D,2) and 12*binomial(D,3). Thus lattice-minus-cube differences are -D/2 for squares and -(9/2)D(D-2) for six-cycles. The graphs are compared at the same degree, not the same dimension.

label: proof
statement: Orient a diamond as 0->a,b->c and let simple random walk use its underlying undirected unit-edge graph. Its probability of returning to 0 at two steps is 1/2, although a forward-only walk has return probability zero. Thus bond orientation in oriented percolation does not justify forbidding backward steps in the undirected random-walk spectral-dimension problem.

label: proof
statement: In a finite unit-conductance network between an origin and a target boundary, if m distinct singleton edge cuts separate them, effective resistance is at least m. Every unit flow has current of magnitude one through each cut edge, so its energy is at least m. More generally pairwise edge-disjoint separating cutsets C_j give the lower bound sum_j 1/|C_j|. This alone provides no random IIC bottleneck tail estimate.

label: proof
statement: For a simple undirected circulant graph on Z/nZ, let S contain one representative of each included unordered nonzero generator pair and m=floor(n/2). Its Lovasz theta number is n times the maximum z_0 subject to z_j>=0, sum_{j=0}^m z_j=1, and sum_{j=0}^m z_j*cos(2*pi*j*s/n)=0 for every s in S. Paired Fourier frequencies are aggregated; the zero and even-n self-inverse frequency remain unpaired. This is a rederivation of the LP already described in the cached 2025 source.

label: proof
statement: Include every unordered nonzero generator pair of Z/nZ independently with probability 1/2. Expected Lovasz theta is 3/2 for n=2, 2 for n=3, 9/4 for n=4, and (3+sqrt(5))/2 for n=5. At n=4 the four theta values are 4,2,2,1; at n=5 they are 5,sqrt(5),sqrt(5),1. These finite values do not establish the conjectured large-n asymptotic.

label: proof
statement: For fair random circulants on n vertices set Z=log(theta(G)/sqrt(n)). Vertex transitivity and complement symmetry give E theta(G)/sqrt(n)=E cosh(Z)>=1+E[Z^2]/2. Hence asymptotic expectation ratio one requires E[Z^2]->0. If also E exp(Z)<=exp(sigma_n^2/2) with sigma_n->0, that expectation ratio tends to one. The latter MGF bound is a sufficient hypothesis, not a bound proved for the random graph here.

These are numerical solver checks, not rational feasibility certificates and not proof of a large-n limit.

label: proof
statement: For Bernoulli initial infection probability p on the four-regular tree, two-neighbor bootstrap has complete occupation almost surely for p>1/9 and fails almost surely for p<=1/9. Thus the complete-occupation critical infimum is 1/9. At p=1/9 the probability a specified root remains vacant is 21/32. Directed vacancy messages converge to the largest solution x=q(3x^2-2x^3), q=1-p; the critical largest solution is x=3/4 at q=8/9. This is a tree special case, not the general group characterization.

label: source-limited record or evidence
statement: Two-neighbor bootstrap on the three-regular tree completes almost surely at its critical infimum p=1/2, whereas on the four-regular tree it fails at its critical infimum p=1/9. The latter has positive critical residual vacancy 21/32 at the root. A critical threshold specified as an infimum therefore does not automatically assert occupation at the threshold itself.
